## Problem

`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` sits at **798 lines against the locked 800-LOC hard cap** — two lines of headroom. The next change that adds three lines to it fails CI, and there is no allowlist and no way to raise the limit (`.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked; a contributor change to it fails the build by design).

This is not hypothetical. Change 2359 (`bd66-28a4-fd31-4c9f`) already hit it: the file was 788 on main, 2359 added 45, and CI refused at 833 on all four platforms. That change landed by relocating `run_auto_maintenance` into `event_commit_git.py` and compressing a comment block — which cleared the cap but left the file at 798, so the problem is deferred rather than solved. Several other in-flight changes are growing `src/rebar` modules concurrently.

### What the size test enforces, and where RED begins

`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py::test_no_src_module_over_the_hard_cap` mirrors the CI gate and enforces **only the 800-line hard cap** — it does NOT enforce the 200-500 target. So at 798 it is **already GREEN**, and this work does NOT flip it RED to GREEN; it keeps it GREEN with room to spare. Measured on this tree:

| `gitutil.py` lines | contract test |
|---|---|
| 798 (today, `origin/main`) | PASSES |
| 801 (append three blank lines) | FAILS: "src/rebar file(s) over the 800-LOC hard cap" |
| 373 (after this split) | PASSES |

The RED boundary is therefore exactly **three added lines** away. The proving evidence for this ticket is the measured post-split LOC and the restored headroom, not a RED-to-GREEN transition.

## The seam — it already exists in the file

`gitutil.py`'s own module docstring carves out a self-contained policy essay, "Blocking policy under local git lock contention". That is the boundary: **`gitutil` RUNS a git subprocess; the extracted layer DECIDES what happens when git's own locks are contended.** The dependency runs one way (`gitutil` -> `git_locking`).

### Exactly what moves to `git_locking.py`

Functions: `_store_git_op_lock`, `_store_git_lock_path`, `fetch_coordination_lock`, `_resolve_common_git_dir`, `_acquire_fetch_coord_flock`, `_with_index_lock_retry`, `_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock`, `_augment_lock_exhaustion`, `_is_index_lock_error`, `_is_git_lock_error`, `_jitter`, `_backoff_sleep`, `_lock_backoff_s`, `_lock_retry_budget_s`, `_resolve_tracker_git_dir`.

Module-level state the moved functions read as globals — these MUST travel with their readers or the readers see a stale/absent global: `_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S`, `_INDEX_LOCK_ATTEMPTS`, `_INDEX_LOCK_BACKOFF_S`, `_INDEX_LOCK_BACKOFF_CAP_S`, `_STORE_GIT_LOCK_NAME`, `_STORE_GIT_LOCK_WAIT_S`, `_STORE_GIT_LOCK_POLL_S`, `_FETCH_COORD_LOCK_NAME`, `_FETCH_COORD_WAIT_S`, `_FETCH_COORD_POLL_S`, `_LOCK_PATH_RE`, `_LOCK_REF_RE`, and the two test probes `_retry_probe` / `_reclaim_probe`.

### What stays in `gitutil.py`

`run_git`, `run_git_bounded`, `run_git_write`, `_with_transient_fault_retry` and its `_TRANSIENT_*` tables, `is_transient_object_read_error`, `_is_transient_object_write_error`, `_is_transient_git_fault`, `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT`, `_AUTOMAINT_OFF`, `_ticket_dirs`, `_dir_is_archived`, `path_is_foreign_to_branch`, `discard_unmerged_paths`.

### Re-exports `gitutil` must keep (production importers, enumerated by AST)

Every `from rebar._store.gitutil import <moved name>` in `src/`, found by parsing the import
nodes rather than by eye:

| moved name | production importers |
|---|---|
| `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | `_commands/bridge_repair.py:49`, `_commands/fsck.py:57`, `_commands/fsck_recover.py:20`, `_commands/fsck_repair.py:32`, `_commands/fsck_scan.py:43`, `_commands/tracker_maintenance.py:99` |
| `_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock` | `_commands/fsck_scan.py:43` |
| `_with_index_lock_retry` | `_store/event_commit_git.py:29` |
| `_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S` | `_store/event_append.py:103` |
| `_backoff_sleep`, `_jitter` | `_store/lock.py:71` |
| `fetch_coordination_lock` | `_snapshot/git_fetch.py:23`, `_store/sync.py:52` |

All are covered by re-export and require no change; the check is that every `rebar` module still
imports cleanly.

### Test consumers, split by HOW they depend on a moved name

**(a) `monkeypatch.setattr` on the module object — a mis-target RAISES** (`raising=True` is the
default, and the moved names are deliberately NOT re-exported), so these fail loudly:
`tests/interfaces/store/test_git_contention_9305.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_delete_init_index_lock.py`,
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_index_lock.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_event_append_index_lock.py`,
`tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_index_lock_reclaim_toctou.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_stale_lock_reclaim_write.py`,
`tests/unit/test_fetch_common_dir_coordination.py`.

**(b) `monkeypatch.setattr` whose READER STAYED in `gitutil`** — these must NOT be retargeted:
`tests/unit/store/test_git_outcome.py` patches `"rebar._store.gitutil._backoff_sleep"` in string
form, and `tests/unit/test_gitutil_transient_write_retry.py` patches `gitutil._backoff_sleep` /
`gitutil.run_git`; their readers (`_with_transient_fault_retry`, `run_git_bounded`) stay put.

**(c) `getattr` READ with a silent default — a SECOND vacuity channel, and it does NOT raise.**
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_delete_init_index_lock.py:24` and
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_index_lock.py:22` both do
`_STALE_S = getattr(gitutil, "_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S", 300)`. If the re-export were dropped, these
would silently fall through to the literal `300` instead of failing. Worse, the real constant IS
`300`, so comparing the value proves nothing — the test would look identical either way. The
proof must use a SENTINEL default: `getattr(gitutil, "_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S", sentinel) is not
sentinel`. `tests/interfaces/store/test_event_append_index_lock.py:40` and
`tests/interfaces/store/test_txn_index_lock.py:21` read the same constant through
`event_append`, which re-exports it from `gitutil`, so the same chain must hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` passes (it passes before the work too; it must not regress).
- [ ] `gitutil.py` is within the 200-500 LOC target.
- [ ] The new `git_locking.py` is within the 200-500 LOC target.
- [ ] Every moved function body is byte-identical to its original, shown by a `difflib` comparison of the moved line ranges, not by eye.
- [ ] The retained half of `gitutil.py` differs from its pre-split content only in the docstring and the import block; no executable line changes.
- [ ] The same test set passes before and after the split, with no test moving from passing to failing.
- [ ] Every `monkeypatch.setattr` aimed at a symbol whose reader MOVED is retargeted to `git_locking`.
- [ ] Every `monkeypatch.setattr` aimed at a symbol whose reader STAYED is left on `gitutil`.
- [ ] Each retarget is shown to be load-bearing by the evidence described under Testing.
- [ ] `gitutil`'s production importers require no change, shown by importing every `rebar` module without error.
- [ ] Every `getattr(gitutil, <moved name>, <default>)` READ still resolves on `gitutil`, proven with a sentinel default rather than by comparing the value.

## Testing

- Compare moved line ranges against the new module with `difflib` and show the diff is empty apart from join whitespace — do not eyeball it.
- **`monkeypatch.setattr` is the dangerous part and needs explicit proof.** A patch aimed at the wrong module is **silently vacuous**, not a loud failure: the test still passes while patching nothing. A green suite is NOT evidence. For each retargeted patch, demonstrate it still takes effect by ONE of:
  - **Mis-target probe** — aim the patch at the module the reader left, and show the run fails loudly (`monkeypatch.setattr` defaults to `raising=True`, so a name absent from that module raises `AttributeError`).
  - **Seeded mutant** — for a name that IS still present on both modules (`_backoff_sleep`), seed the behaviour the patch is meant to observe and show the correct target notices it while the old target passes vacuously.
  - **Invocation probe** — for a patch deliberately LEFT on `gitutil`, record calls and assert the patched callable actually fired.
- **`getattr` reads with a default are the second vacuity channel and need a DIFFERENT proof.** They do not raise on a missing name, they fall through — and when the default equals the real value (`300`), the fallback is invisible. Assert with a sentinel default that the name resolves on `gitutil`, and that it is the same object `git_locking` holds.
- Grep for the module path and every moved symbol **as a STRING** (`monkeypatch.setattr`, `getattr`, `importlib`, patch targets, docs references). An LSP cannot see these, so a semantic search returning nothing is not evidence of absence.
- Run `make lint` (including the complexity ratchet: `new=0 increased=0`) and `make typecheck` to zero, plus `check_comment_hygiene`, `check_raw_git_writes`, `check_wall_clock_asserts`.
